## 1. The one who was dead and was given life  (`#the-one-given-life-and-light`)

Cited ayat: 6:122

> **6:122** أَوَمَن كَانَ مَيْتًا فَأَحْيَيْنَٰهُ وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُۥ نُورًا يَمْشِى بِهِۦ فِى ٱلنَّاسِ كَمَن مَّثَلُهُۥ فِى ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ لَيْسَ بِخَارِجٍ مِّنْهَا كَذَٰلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِلْكَٰفِرِينَ مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (6:122): The ayah asks whether one who was dead, and whom God gave life and made for him a light by which he walks among people, is like one whose similitude is in the darknesses, from which he does not come out.

**c2** (6:122): The ayah says that thus what they used to do was made to seem fair to the disbelievers.

### One-minute summary

The ayah asks whether one who was dead and whom God gave life and made a light for, by which he walks among people, is like one whose similitude is in the darknesses [c1]. It adds that what they used to do was made to seem fair to the disbelievers [c2].

### Complete story

The ayah asks a question [c1]. It asks whether one who was dead, and whom God gave life and made for him a light by which he walks among people, is like one whose similitude is in the darknesses, from which he does not come out [c1]. The ayah says that thus what they used to do was made to seem fair to the disbelievers [c2].

### Deep study

The ayah is a question, and it sets states side by side: given life and light, and darknesses from which there is no coming out [c1]. The first person walks among people by the light, and the ayah uses the word for a similitude (mathal) of the one in the darknesses [c1]. The ayah closes by saying what was made to seem fair to the disbelievers [c2].

### Kids mode

The ayah asks about one who was dead and whom God gave life and a light to walk among people by [c1]. It asks whether he is like one who is in the darknesses and does not come out [c1].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah sets life and light beside darknesses from which there is no coming out [c1]. Another reading is that the ayah ends by saying that what they used to do was made to seem fair to the disbelievers [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the one who was dead and the one in the darknesses are; the ayah names no one.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later commentary names the persons it takes them to be; this draft does not repeat or vouch for them.
- Not established: whether dead is meant of the body or of the state of belief; this draft keeps the ayah's word and leaves the sense open.
- The ayah uses the word for a similitude (mathal) of the one in the darknesses, and puts the whole as a question.
